tagline: Down the neck to a free ferry, and back around.
intro: River Road leaves Route 3 near Litwalton and runs down the neck between the Rappahannock and the Western Branch of the Corrotoman, through Somers and on to Ottoman. There the road gives way to water, and a free ferry carries the loop across the Western Branch to Merry Point Road.
From Lancaster it runs Mary Ball Road to Kilmarnock and White Stone, then Irvington Road back north through Irvington and Pitmans Corner. It crosses itself in Kilmarnock.

moments.title: Belle Isle State Park
moments.text: West of Somers, a park on a peninsula of tidewater marsh between Deep Creek and Morattico Creek, on land patented in 1652 and known in those years as Powell's Quarter.

moments.title: Merry Point Ferry
moments.text: At Ottoman the byway crosses the Western Branch of the Corrotoman on a free ferry, which lands on Merry Point Road on the far side.

moments.title: Christ Church
moments.text: The only colonial Virginia church still keeping its original high-backed pews, and John Carter, who paid for the first church here, lies in the grounds beside four of his five wives.

practical: The Merry Point Ferry is a free VDOT ferry that does not run every day of the week, and wind, weather and tides can halt it; Virginia 511 gives its status.
